articles.title: When Automatic Configuration Leaves Questions Unanswered
articles.excerpt: When Automatic Configuration Leaves Questions Unanswered Automatic configuration makes developer products easier to use. A platform might create resources, select default settings, or handle setup ste…
articles.body: When Automatic Configuration Leaves Questions Unanswered Automatic configuration makes developer products easier to use. A platform might create resources, select default settings, or handle setup steps that developers would otherwise perform manually. This reduces the amount of work required to get started. But automation can also leave developers uncertain about what happened behind the scenes, what remains their responsibility, and what they need to verify before moving forward. The challenge is not automation itself. It is understanding the boundary between what the product handles automatically and what the developer must still do. When Automation Creates Uncertainty Imagine a developer using a deployment platform.
articles.author: Nwajichukwu Goodness

articles.title: No Sqwakie server in the middle: how Sqwakie keeps a team's coding agents in sync with a signed, replicated log
articles.excerpt: Sqwakie is a coordination layer for teams that run Claude Code and Codex agents on several machines: shared channels, questions one agent can put to another, kanban boards, and a live dashboard of wha…
articles.body: Sqwakie is a coordination layer for teams that run Claude Code and Codex agents on several machines: shared channels, questions one agent can put to another, kanban boards, and a live dashboard of what every agent is doing. The obvious way to build that is a hosted backend that every machine talks to. Sqwakie doesn't have one. Team data travels machine to machine, directly where the network allows and through an encrypted relay that can't read it where it doesn't, and it never sits on our servers, except on machines you rent from us (a rented machine is a VM in our provider account that joins your team like any other machine). This post walks through how that works, using only what the public repository documents.
articles.author: Alex Carney

articles.title: Modeling "will this part fit?" as code: a replacement-rule validator for HVAC capacitors
articles.excerpt: Most "does this part fit?" questions in e-commerce get answered with a lookup table: part A replaces part B because somebody typed it into a spreadsheet. That breaks down for commodity electrical part…
articles.body: Most "does this part fit?" questions in e-commerce get answered with a lookup table: part A replaces part B because somebody typed it into a spreadsheet. That breaks down for commodity electrical parts, where thousands of part numbers are really just a handful of ratings. For those, it's better to encode the substitution rules and check any candidate against the original part. Run capacitors in air conditioners and heat pumps are a clean example. The label on the old part tells you nearly everything you need, and the rules for a safe replacement are short: Capacitance (µF, also printed MFD) must match exactly. A dual-run label like 45 + 5 MFD means 45 µF for the compressor (HERM) and 5 µF for the fan. The tolerance printed next to it (±5% or ±6%) is the normal manufacturing range.

articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

articles.body: Just imagine… a nice, clean homescreen with no ads, thanks to Claude. | Image: cleanyourtv Vibe coding has reached TVs. Social media is awash with posts from people using LLMs and open-source tools to remove ads and tracking, trim bloat so the OS runs faster, and even completely change the look and organization of their homescreens. While a lot of it is fun - one user turned their TV homescreen into a Pokémon town - I think there's a level of frustration behind it, too. And TV companies should take notice. Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.
articles.author: Charles Q. Choi

articles.title: Rocket Lab launches 3 'Hawk' satellites to orbit to gather signals intelligence
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 21), the 19th mission of the year for the California-based company.
articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.
articles.author: Mike Wall

articles.title: Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: Space is a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. It’s therefore critical to maintain a safe and clean orbital environment.
articles.body: David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects . While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.
articles.author: David Zamora

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 23 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Andromeda in Southern Spring Explanation: Looking toward the north from Mullion, New South Wales, Australia, the Andromeda Galaxy never gets more than a few degrees above the horizon. During the southern hemisphere spring, Andromeda is highest in the sky around midnight though. And in this telephoto scene from October 10/11, multiple exposures were used to reveal the spiral galaxy in tantalizing detail as it climbed above rolling Australian hills.
